scheme_name: Traffic Police Challan Abhay Yojana-2026 (cabinet-approved, not yet notified)
note: Maharashtra's transport department proposed a one-time settlement in August 2025: two- and three-wheeler owners would pay 25% of pending dues (effectively a 75% waiver), with a 50% waiver for violations cleared within 15 days, and smaller waivers for costlier vehicles, against roughly ₹2,500 crore outstanding statewide (₹1,817 crore in Mumbai alone since 2020). That August 2025 proposal was superseded: on 4 November 2026 the Maharashtra Cabinet (CM Devendra Fadnavis) approved a different, smaller scheme — the Traffic Police Challan Abhay Yojana-2026, a one-time concession of up to 20% (not 75%/50%) on pending compoundable e-challans — reported independently by UNI, Punekar News, Spinny and News18 Marathi. As reported, it has three phases: (1) up to 20% off pending compoundable challans issued 21 January-31 October 2026, usable for 30 days once a notification is issued; (2) a standing 20% early-payment discount, for one year, on any challan issued from 1 November 2026 onward if paid within 45 days of issue; (3) up to 20% off pending compoundable fines for challans issued 30 January 2019-20 January 2026 where court recovery has already started, usable for 30 days once notified. No G.O./notification number is cited by any report, and none describes the notification as issued yet. A direct check of Maharashtra's official GR portal (gr.maharashtra.gov.in) today found no Transport Department resolution matching this scheme. Because the Cabinet itself 'approved the issuance of a notification to formally implement the scheme' (per Punekar News) rather than issuing an order with immediate effect, and because Phase 1 and Phase 3's windows only start to run once that notification is published — with press (7 November 2026 coverage) explicitly stating no start date is known yet — this stays recorded as a proposal, not announced/live: no discount can actually be claimed yet, and a window start date is not something we can state without inventing it (CONTENT_STANDARDS rule 9). Status will move to 'announced' once a notification is published and a real window date exists. Until then, the only settlement route is a National Lok Adalat sitting. Confirm current status on the Transport Department or Maharashtra Traffic Police site before expecting any discount. Re-checked 25 November 2026: a direct check of gr.maharashtra.gov.in's Government Resolutions section again found no Transport Department resolution matching this scheme, and a fresh web search surfaced only recaps of the 4 November 2026 cabinet approval and the transporters'-pushback coverage already recorded here (UNI, Punekar News, Spinny) — no notification number, no start date, no rate change. Status remains 'proposal'.
